resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lookout lists (firelookout.com, idahofirelookouts.com, Forest Lookouts) name the Kaniksu National Forest. The University of Idaho photo records place the point in the Priest River Experimental Forest, and one record names the Priest Creek Experimental Forest headquarters. The story gives both names and does not choose between them.

The lists date the cabin to about 1918 and a July 1918 photo shows lumber packed in for a cabin, but a university photo dated 1917 is already titled Experiment Station Lookout. The story gives c.1918 as the start and notes the 1917 photo; the first structure on the point is not settled by these sources.

notes_for_editor: Main open question is the forest name: the University of Idaho photo records are the only sources that name the Priest River Experimental Forest, and they are photo catalogue entries, not a forest history. The cabin removal has no separate date, so the story says it is undated and no removed event is kept. Experimental Point is named only in the U of I photo records (cites 5 and 6), not on the lookout pages, so the story cites 6 for it. No staffing, fire or access statements were found, so none is written. Record kind 'ground' follows the FFLA list; the firelookout.com text (platform atop a frame cabin) might fit another kind, not changed. The U of I photos dated 1917, July 1918 and 1928 are noted here but not added as photos because no image download URL was checked. No photo of the cabin itself was found.
